runs.name: Japan Tobacco Inc.
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **¥7,230** (TSE 2914, close 2026-10-09; Tokyo shut 2026-10-12; the intraday ¥7,245 of 2026-10-13 not used) and ADR **$22.87** (OTC close 2026-10-12), aggregator, flagged; **1 ADS = 1/2 share** on The Bank of New York Mellon's F-6EF for the unsponsored programme (2016-10-07, accession 0001019155-16-000725; the F-6 prints no ticker, so JAPAY linked to the ratio by price against JAPAF). Shares **1,776,000,893** (2,000,000,000 issued less 223,999,107 treasury at 2026-06-30, Semi-annual Securities Report; 1,775,800,463 at 2025-12-31) = cap **¥12,840bn** (about $81.2bn); sovereign **4.14%** (JGB 30Y, Ministry of Finance jgbcme.csv, 2026-10-08), a CONVENTION of this run for a stream earned in a basket of currencies and reported in yen, the US 5.60% shown beside. Not an SEC registrant (`cover_shares.py` 'NOT AN SEC REGISTRANT'): every figure by hand from the English Annual Securities Report for the 41st term (FY2025, filed 2026-03-23, posted under Rule 12g3-2(b)), the six earlier Annual Securities Reports, the Semi-annual Securities Report January to June 2026, the Integrated Report 2026, the FY2025 results presentation (2026-02-12) and the BREAK and Moro release (2026-07-23). Not read: the 2026 Notice of Convocation (downloaded), notes 14, 19 and 32 in full, the prices of the 2017-19 deals; Russia's profit and the maintenance share of capital spending are not disclosed. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the report's Business Description, Business and Other Risks and Management Analysis, as the overnight brief directs. In the window: Vector Group bought October 2024 (about ¥344.6bn, cash); the pharmaceutical business and the Torii shares transferred to Shionogi (September and December 2025); the Canadian CCAA plans implemented 2025-08-29 (provision ¥375.6bn in 2024, ¥161.3bn unpaid at 2026-06-30); BREAK and Moro trademarks signed 2026-07-22 for EUR 176m, unclosed. **Q1 IN**: Tobacco 99.2% of five-year segment adjusted operating profit (¥3,884.6bn of ¥3,915.6bn), combustibles about 96% of tobacco core revenue; industry volume -2.7% in 2025, price/mix +7.0%, +6.2%, +8.0%, +10.8% in 2022-25 with share rising; the new formats and Russia passed to Q2. **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: for the castle, pricing power through the inflation with rising share and excellent returns (2025 adjusted operating profit ¥902.2bn on tangible equity of about ¥768bn); against, in Japan, where heated tobacco arrived in force, JT's share of the whole market fell from 48.7% (2019) to 40.8% (2025) and its heated share was 15.7% in Q4 2025; its RRP loses money at brand contribution, with about ¥800bn to be spent in 2026-28 to reach break-even; Russia, 14.3% of revenue through one distributor (Megapolis), which JT 'is unable to reasonably estimate' and PMI calls 'impossible to predict'; BAT: 'it cannot be predicted whether regulations will permit the marketing' of the new formats. NATURE because the insiders decline to write the forecast down (a rolling three-year plan for 'increasing uncertainties'); no research pass. Q3 to Q12 not reached; Q12 (tobacco) not reached, its facts recorded after the stop. After the stop, recorded not weighed: inventories, mostly leaf, ¥563bn (2021) to ¥1,060bn (2025), absorbing ¥449bn in 2022-25, why adjusted operating profit rose about 48% while owner cash did not; ¥166.2bn of cash restricted in Iran; no buyback programme in 2021-25; payout target about 75% (85.0% in 2025); deals RJR Nabisco non-US 1999, Gallaher 2007, Katokichi 2008, Natural American Spirit non-US 2016, Vector 2024, all cash; goodwill ¥2,923bn, 58-77% of equity over 2015-25; **integrity facts recorded, not judged**: 2025 bonus targets beaten widely (adjusted operating profit ¥901.3bn against a ¥746.0bn target), the featured profit measure redefined from 2026 to exclude the Canadian annual payments, business in sanctioned countries (Russia, Iran), the chairman from March 2026 a former Administrative Vice Minister of Finance while the Ministry holds 37.55% and a statutory veto. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash after the company's own tax, all capital spending, lease principal and minority dividends, 2021-25 equity basis as reported ¥473.6, 361.8, 423.5, 450.7, 324.2bn; central series all-equity, the 2025 Canadian cash added back (the unpaid ¥161.3bn counted as debt), acquisitions deducted, ¥476.0, 363.1, 410.0, 154.1, 455.9bn, average **¥371.8bn**, growth **-1.07% a year** (a decline, carried as the bottom); net debt ¥822.9bn at 2026-06-30 with the Canadian liability; **range ¥4,713 to ¥5,149 a share** ($14.90 to $16.28 an ADS) against ¥7,230; no case earns the floor (2.81% to 3.05% at the price; ten percent would need 18.4% growth a year for ten years); fair price beneath the stop **¥1,690 all-equity** (about $5.34 an ADS), ¥2,352 equity-only; beside: the literal window ¥1,314 to ¥4,623, the US rate ¥3,328 to ¥3,632, Iranian cash not counted ¥4,620 to ¥5,055; not armed (box not OUT at Q7). Balance sheets 2015-25: interest-bearing debt ¥255bn to ¥1,679bn, net cash to net debt ¥848bn (note 33); ratings A2, A+ negative, AA, AA+. Competitors: the report names PMI (10-K) and BAT (20-F) and no other rival individually (China National Tobacco excluded from its ranking, not an SEC filer); ten-year operating margin 2016-25 JT 22.7%, PMI 37.8%, BAT 23.6% (BAT includes the £27.3bn 2023 impairment and its Canadian charge; about 35-40% in normal years), JT at about two-thirds of PMI's margin every year. Contamination declared by the analyst: a ticker-filtered listing of `Test Runs/` printed the 2026-07-15 JAPAY file name (not opened), the session's FJTSY and FUJIY commit subjects and a memory index line; none used. Commits through 622c65a2. Citations: the analyst's check PASS (35 ids); the dispatcher's adjacency script 35 distinct ids resolved, 0 E-ids, 21 adjacent fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. Fetching note for the operator: jt.com and jti.co.jp return 403 to Git Bash curl, Python and WebFetch; Windows' own curl with browser headers and a Referer works. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q1 against Q2 for an incumbent under format substitution: Q1's fast-change routing and test 6 against Q2's 'a castle whose future cannot be judged'; a second analyst could close at Q1 with the same box, or pass Q2 and close OUT at Q7 on price; (2) whether geographic clusters reported to the board inside one segment are parts (EMA, holding Russia, is the largest); (3) no treatment for a non-deciding part whose future cannot be judged (Russia); (4) IFRS 16 has no finance/operating lease split for the all-equity convention, and no rule for unremittable cash (Iran) or a settlement liability carried as a financial liability (Canada); (5) no rule for the earnings currency of a multi-currency earner reporting in yen; (6) 'purchases stop after year ten' read for both ends of the range; (7) the template gives Step 0 no slot for Q4's balance sheets when the file closes early, and its accession line cannot be met by a non-SEC filer.
runs.narr: Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): Tobacco decides (99.2% of five-year segment profit, combustibles about 96% of tobacco revenue); pricing power through the inflation with rising share and excellent returns, but in Japan, the one market where heated tobacco arrived in force, JT's share fell from 48.7% to 40.8% (2019-25), its RRP loses money with about ¥800bn to be spent to 2028 to break even, and Russia, 14.3% of revenue through one distributor, the company says it cannot estimate. Vector Group bought 2024; pharmaceuticals sold to Shionogi 2025; Canadian settlement implemented 2025. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash average ¥371.8bn all-equity, growth -1.07% a year, range ¥4,713 to ¥5,149 at the 4.14% JGB against ¥7,230, no case earns the floor, fair ¥1,690 all-equity (¥2,352 equity-only), not armed. After the stop: leaf inventories nearly doubled 2021-25; ¥166bn cash restricted in Iran; integrity facts recorded, not judged: bonus targets beaten widely, the featured profit measure redefined to exclude the Canadian payments, business in Russia and Iran, a former Vice Minister of Finance as chairman while the Ministry holds 37.55%.
